_comment: LINEDOWN — alternate MODULE candidates for the at-risk AI-SRV-G4 memory line.
ALL PRICING IS ILLUSTRATIVE. `pricePerUnit`, `extendedTotal`, premiums and discounts are
plausible figures chosen for the demo, NOT quoted market data. The AGENTS track may replace
them with live Tavily results. Nothing downstream should present them as fact.
MODULE vs DIE: every candidate is a complete 288-pin DDR5 RDIMM ASSEMBLY from a different
module manufacturer. This is a module-level alternate. No candidate substitutes DRAM die
inside a module, and no narration should imply that it does. HBM capacity cannibalisation is
the cause of the shortage, not a thing we are sourcing — there are no alternates for HBM.
PART NUMBERS: Micron / Samsung / SK hynix MPNs are real market part numbers for 64GB 2Rx4
DDR5-4800 RDIMMs. The V-color MPN and the broker lot code are format-correct but illustrative.
FIELD SHAPES: `specs` is the string map the UI renders and that candidate.added carries
(schema: Record<string,string>). `specsNormalized` is the typed object the AGENTS qualification
engine compares field-by-field against qvl.json `requirements`. Keep the two in sync.
DESIGNED OUTCOMES — these four exist to drive four different, non-overlapping rejections:
cand-01 cheapest, spec-compatible, NOT on QVL  -> Engineering BLOCK  (beat 4)
cand-02 broker, qualified MPN, too-good price   -> COUNTERFEIT catch  (beat 5)
cand-03 qualified, in stock, slightly pricier   -> APPROVED WINNER    (beat 6)
cand-04 qualified, but 14-week lead             -> SCHEDULE reject
cand-02 deliberately carries the QUALIFIED INCUMBENT MPN, so it PASSES the QVL lookup. QVL
answers 'was this part tested here'; it cannot answer 'is this physical module genuine'. That
is why beats 4 and 5 are two independent findings and must not be collapsed into one.

atRiskPart.reason: Supplier cut allocation 40% — DDR5 wafer starts reallocated to HBM
atRiskPart.plain: We are 4,608 memory sticks short of what the factory needs in 11 days.

candidates.traceability: manufacturer C of C available; full lot traceability
candidates.specCompareToRequirements: MATCH on all five platform requirements — zero mismatches
candidates.outcomeReason: Not on platform QVL for AI-SRV-G4 (QVL-G4-2026.08-rev-D). Spec-compatible on all five requirements, but EVAL-G4-0412 is incomplete — no RDIMM margin or thermal validation report, no 24-slot 1DPC loading data, not covered by shipped BIOS G4-BIOS-1.3.2 memory reference code.
candidates.plain: The cheapest offer — about $209,000 less across the whole order, and the spec sheet is an exact match. But this supplier's memory was never actually tested in this server. It fits on paper and nobody has ever run 24 of them in one machine at full load. Could take the cluster down.
candidates.notes: This is a genuine, reputable module manufacturer. 'Not on the QVL' is a statement about what was tested on THIS platform, not an accusation about product quality — say it that way on stage. Its path to qualification is real: 40 samples plus a thermal chamber slot, ~6 weeks to a signed report.

candidates.vendor: Micron (offered via broker — Pacific Rim Components Ltd., HK)
candidates.source: Open-market broker, non-franchised — ex-stock Hong Kong
candidates.traceability: NONE — no certificate of conformance, no manufacturer traceability, single lot, single date code, seller will not name the original buyer
candidates.qvlNote: The MPN IS on the QVL (validation report MV-G4-0244) and this candidate therefore PASSES the QVL lookup. The qualification covers the part number, not this seller's physical lot. Do not let the qualification engine clear it.
candidates.outcomeReason: Counterfeit / remarked indicators confirmed on lot PRC-24817 — six independent top-marking failures. Non-franchised supply chain, no certificate of conformance, no traceability to the module manufacturer. Referred to ERAI and added to AVL blacklist.
redFlags: 4,608 pcs ex-stock of a part the factory itself is on allocation for — the quantity alone is not credible
28.6% below our own contract price in a rising market
exactly the quantity we need, which implies the offer was built around our shortage
single lot, single date code across the whole quantity
no C of C, no traceability, 100% prepayment, no warranty
'excess from a cancelled hyperscaler order' — the standard cover story
candidates.plain: A middleman offering the exact part we are short of, immediately, 29% below what we normally pay. Nobody has that stock. The labels on these sticks were sanded off and reprinted — they are not the part they claim to be, and we cannot tell what is actually inside them.
candidates.notes: Looks $364,262 cheaper than the winner. Taking it would mean scrapping the lot and rebuilding 192 nodes — roughly $1.07M — so the decision to refuse is about $702,000 better, not worse. That inversion is the point of beat 5.

candidates.source: Franchised distributor — 5,100 pcs ex-stock, ARO 5 working days
candidates.traceability: full — manufacturer C of C, lot and date-code traceability, franchised chain of custody
candidates.outcomeReason: Qualified on QVL-G4-2026.08-rev-D (validation report MV-G4-0288), franchised stock covering the full 4,608 pcs, ARO 5 working days inside the 11-day kit date, human approval recorded.
candidates.plain: The winner. $17.80 more per stick — about $82,000 more in total — but it is in stock now, it arrives in five working days, it has been fully tested in this exact server, and it comes with paperwork an auditor can follow. Against $1.79M a day of risk if the factory stops, the extra $82,000 is noise.
candidates.notes: A true drop-in MODULE replacement: same 288-pin RDIMM, 31.25mm height, 2Rx4, same 1DPC population rules, no board change, no BIOS change, no die substitution. This is the only candidate that satisfies all four gates at once — qualified, genuine, available, and affordable enough to defend.

candidates.source: Franchised distributor — factory order, no stock
candidates.traceability: full — manufacturer C of C, franchised chain of custody
candidates.outcomeReason: Schedule infeasible — 14-week factory lead time against an 11-day Build-1 kit date. No franchised or bonded stock located. Rejected on schedule only.
candidates.plain: Fully approved for this server and slightly cheaper than the winner — but it would not arrive for over three months, and the factory needs it next week.
candidates.notes: A SCHEDULE reject, not a quality reject. Keep that distinction in any narration: there is nothing wrong with this part and it stays on the QVL. It exists in the set to show the desk weighing time as a hard constraint, not just price.

gateResults.cand-04: passed gates 1 and 2, failed gate 3 — schedule

decisionSummary.plain: Four offers, four different reasons they do or do not work. Only one was tested on the server, genuine, in stock, and defensible on price. Finding it took 2.5 minutes instead of days of email, and the factory never stopped.
